claim: folder-matches-a-shape refuses a folder opening with the name of the page above it, and cannot see that fault where the folder above holds more than two pages. Whether the check looks at all is decided by how many siblings happen to sit beside that page, which has nothing to do with the shape being judged. So a folder wrongly named is let through for as long as its parent is crowded, and begins refusing every change touching it the moment an unrelated removal drops the count to one. The fault surfaces on whoever is working there, at a time chosen by someone else's landing.

evidence:
Read on 2026-09-21 against this checkout, from a migration that hit it.

Where the count enters. `pairedIn` in check/code/pages/folder-matches-a-shape/folder-matches-a-shape.check-code.decision.code.ts opens `const [one, two] = pages` and then `if (one === undefined || pages.length > 2) return []`. Its answer becomes the `names` of a folder. `refusalsAt` asks `openingWith(named, holds(namingFolderOf(folder, holds, heldNames)).names)`, so where the folder above holds three pages or more the name list is empty and `openingWith` matches nothing.

What happened. `alan/book/pages/all-about-alan/sections/` held `notes.book-section.ts` beside a `notes/` folder of its children, and also held `journal.book-section.ts` and one more page. Every removal inside `sections/notes/` landed clean through 15:58. At 16:00:58 commit 4fc3f5dbe5d took `journal.book-section.ts` away, which left `sections/` holding one page. From the next apply onward every change touching `sections/notes` was refused with `this folder opens with notes, what the page above it is named`.

That the shape itself did not move. `sections/notes.book-section.ts` was beside `sections/notes/` before that removal and after it. Nothing about the folder or the page changed. The check's own code last changed at 13:53, before the removals that landed clean. What moved was the number of pages beside the one being judged.

Who it lands on. Three agents were removing pages under that folder at the time, none of them working on `journal`. All three were refused at once, on work that had been landing all afternoon, by a fault none of them made.

What was done about it. The removals were landed with `break-the-glass`, the reason said in the calls, because the whole folder was being emptied within the hour and renaming it would have churned every remaining page's path to reach a shape with no future. That is a way around this one case rather than a mend.

What is unmeasured. How many folders in this repository open with the name of the page above them and are unrefused today because that page has three or more siblings. Whether two is the right number for what `pairedIn` is otherwise for, or whether the name list should be worked out somewhere that does not go through it.
